name: Highlands 27

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from the street side, with the residence set well back from the road amid dense juniper and pine tree coverage|The approach to the structure is largely screened by the tree canopy, limiting direct sightlines from the front|A light-colored structure is visible at the upper-left portion of the frame, partially obscured by surrounding trees|The significant tree density between the road and the residence creates a long, partially obscured approach for any responding unit.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, revealing the main residence as a single-story light-colored structure with a complex multi-section roofline, accompanied by a smaller detached dark-roofed structure to its left|The buildings sit on a relatively open sandy terrain clearing surrounded on all sides by dense juniper and pine trees|A dirt driveway loop is visible wrapping around the structures|No fencing, gates, or above-ground utility features are visible from this perspective.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, with the residence visible in the right-center of the frame exhibiting a dark multi-gabled roofline and light exterior walls|The rear of the property slopes upward away from the structure into dense tree cover with no visible rear access route or secondary drive|The terrain behind the residence rises noticeably, with trees packed tightly up to the rear of the building footprint|No rear doors, decks, or utility features are clearly distinguishable from this angle.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, with the main residence and a smaller detached structure visible at the right-center of the frame set in a clearing among dense juniper trees|The terrain across the left side of the parcel is open sandy desert with scattered trees and no visible structures, fencing, or secondary access routes|The detached structure sits to the left of the main residence with open ground between them|Tree screening on the left side limits sightlines to the structures from that approach.

considerations: The residence is set well back from the road on a large parcel with a single driveway approach that winds through dense juniper and pine tree coverage, limiting visibility and creating a long approach for emergency vehicles. Dense tree cover surrounds the structure on all sides including the rear, where terrain rises steeply, making rear and perimeter access on foot difficult. A detached structure is present to the left of the main residence and would require separate access consideration. The open sandy terrain around the clearing may support off-road vehicle movement in dry conditions, but the surrounding tree density constrains staging options to the cleared area near the driveway loop.
clarifications: Does the driveway have sufficient clearance width and overhead height for a fire apparatus or ambulance along its full length? Is the detached structure locked or does it have a separate entry point? Are there any gates or access controls on the driveway that would impede emergency vehicle entry? What is the surface material of the driveway loop — compacted gravel, dirt, or paved — and is it suitable for heavy vehicle loads? Are there any propane tanks, fuel storage, or utility shutoffs on the property, and if so, where are they located relative to the structures?
